codeReview.summary: Clean, correct fix. All 14 extended PS/2 scancodes updated to QEMU key number convention (base | 0x80). Arithmetic verified: every value is the original PS/2 Set 1 base scancode OR'd with 0x80. Numpad keys correctly retain their non-extended base codes, so numpad vs. navigation/arrow key disambiguation now works as intended. Comments inline with each entry clearly document the derivation (e.g., '// Extended: 0x48 | 0x80'). Tests updated for all 10 previously-tested keys (4 arrow, 6 nav) and 4 new tests added for ControlRight, AltRight, NumpadEnter, NumpadDivide. No functional issues found.

issues.description: Top-of-file doc comment says 'Maps KeyboardEvent.code to PS/2 Set 1 scancodes' and the SCANCODE_MAP JSDoc says the same. Now that extended keys use QEMU key numbers (base | 0x80) rather than raw PS/2 scan codes, this is slightly misleading. Consider updating to mention 'QEMU key numbers (PS/2 Set 1 based, with 0x80 bit for extended keys)' for accuracy.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The SCANCODE_MAP now uses two different encoding conventions: raw PS/2 Set 1 scancodes for standard keys, and QEMU key numbers (base | 0x80) for extended keys. This dual convention is not documented in AGENTS.md. The distinction matters for any future key mapping work — a developer adding new extended keys (e.g., right Windows key, multimedia keys) needs to know to apply the 0x80 bit.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/input.ts lines 108-145: standard keys use raw PS/2 codes (e.g., ControlLeft: 0x1D) while extended keys use QEMU key numbers (e.g., ControlRight: 0x9D). The inline comments explain the derivation per-entry but there's no top-level documentation of the convention.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The frontend-worker SKILL.md keyboard input section says 'Map KeyboardEvent.code to QEMU scancodes (PS/2 Set 1)' without mentioning the 0x80 bit convention for extended keys. This could lead future workers to repeat the original bug (using raw PS/2 codes for extended keys).
sharedStateObservations.evidence: SKILL.md 'For keyboard input' section: 'Map KeyboardEvent.code to QEMU scancodes (PS/2 Set 1)'. Should specify that extended keys (arrow, nav, right modifiers, NumpadEnter, NumpadDivide) require the 0x80 bit OR'd onto the base scancode.

summary: Pass. All 14 extended scancodes correctly updated with verified arithmetic (base | 0x80). Tests comprehensive — 2 existing tests updated, 4 new tests added. No bugs, no missed edge cases. One non-blocking documentation nit: source comments and SKILL.md could clarify the dual encoding convention (raw PS/2 for standard keys, QEMU key numbers with 0x80 bit for extended keys).
